answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by gating every identity behind a costly admission proof, so each clone must pay real compute to enter. New agents arrive at the harbor through a single registration jetty, where their signed keys are checked against the on-ledger registry and duplicated claims are rejected outright. The network's consensus pulse re-verifies identity standing each epoch, so a fleet of rented fakes loses attestation weight the moment their rented keys rotate or lapse. Persistent honest agents keep earning, while ephemeral accounts fade.
